items.t: Said New Mexico's tax system is difficult, confusing, and not fair or simple.
items.q: “It’s difficult, it’s confusing, and it’s certainly not fair or simple,” State Sen. William Sharer, R-Farmington, said during a news conference Wednesday.

items.t: Said New Mexico could eliminate almost every tax it currently levies by reforming the way it collects the gross receipts tax.
items.q: Sharer claimed New Mexico could eliminate almost every tax currently levied by reforming the way it collects the gross receipts tax.

items.t: Said the personal income tax, corporate income tax, compensating tax, vehicle excise tax, insurance premium tax and about a hundred other taxes would go away under his proposal.
items.q: “No personal income tax, no corporate income tax, no compensating tax, no vehicle excise tax, no insurance premium tax and about a hundred other taxes go away,” Sharer said.

items.t: Cited a University of New Mexico study finding that a 2 percent gross receipts tax would generate more revenue than existing taxes if all exemptions, deductions and credits were eliminated.
items.q: Sharer cited a study by Lee Reynis at the University of New Mexico Bureau of Business and Economic Research that found a 2 percent GRT would generate more revenue than existing taxes do

items.t: Said that eliminating the more than 300 exemptions, deductions and credits would let the gross receipts tax pay all state and local government expenses at current funding levels without spending cuts.
items.q: Currently, Sharer said, there are more than 300 exemptions, deductions and credits. If these were eliminated, the GRT would be sufficient to pay all the expenses of the state and local governments at current funding levels

items.t: Said it is inexplicable that a district court discovered a new definition of marriage in New Mexico law, which he said has not changed in over a century.
items.q: It is inexplicable how a district court just today discovered a new definition of marriage in our laws, when our marriage law has not been changed in over a century," Sharer said.

items.t: Said it is up to the state's Legislature, with the governor's consent, to make laws, not county clerks or district judges.
items.q: Sen. William Sharer of Farmington, said it is up to the state's Legislature, with the consent of the governor, to make laws -- not its county clerks or district judges.

record.t: Was first elected to the New Mexico State Senate in 2000 and now serves on its Corporations & Transportation and Conservation committees.
record.q: He was first elected to the New Mexico State Senate in 2000.  He now serves on the committees, Corporations & Transportation and Conservation committees.
